issues.legal_issue: A review of an appealable judgment cannot be used to rehear the dispute or correct an alleged error that is not self-evident on the record.
material_facts: The High Court reviewed its judgment in a second appeal and reversed the result, relying on the view that a separate suit was barred because leave to sue later had not been obtained.
The earlier plaint referred to the agreement for sale and expressly reserved the right to bring a suit for specific performance.
Whether the separate specific-performance suit was barred was not relevant to the suit seeking cancellation of the later sale deed.
The asserted error required examination of the pleadings and reasoning; it was not an error apparent on the face of the record.
issues.conclusion: The review was outside the permissible scope of review jurisdiction. The Supreme Court set aside the review order and restored the judgment in the second appeal.
issues.legal_principle: Section 114 CPC is read with Order XLVII Rule 1 CPC, which permits review on discovery of new and important matter or evidence unavailable despite due diligence, an error apparent on the face of the record, or another sufficient reason. Review is not an appeal in disguise and cannot be used to rehear a dispute or correct an error on the merits. An error is not apparent if establishing it requires a long or debatable process of reasoning. The Court relied on Thungabhadra Industries Ltd. v. Government of Andhra Pradesh, Meera Bhanja v. Nirmala Kumari Choudhary, Aribam Tuleshwar Sharma v. Aribam Pishak Sharma, Shivdeo Singh v. State of Punjab, Satyanarayan Laxminarayan Hegde v. Mallikarjun Bhavanappa Tirumale, and Parsion Devi v. Sumiri Devi.

predicates.review_application_after_appealable_judg: A party applied to the court that issued an appealable judgment to review it.
predicates.alleged_error_requires_reasoning_or_rehe: The alleged error could be established only by examining and reasoning through the dispute rather than by merely looking at the record.
predicates.new_material_unavailable_despite_due_dil: The review applicant relied on new and important material that could not have been obtained or produced earlier despite due diligence.
predicates.self_evident_record_error: The alleged error was immediately apparent from the record without a lengthy or debatable process of reasoning.

issues.definition: When a party seeks review of an appealable judgment and the alleged error requires reasoning or rehearing, rather than resting on qualifying new material or a self-evident record error, the review must be refused.

issues.legal_issue: A supposed bar arising from a separate suit cannot support review of a judgment in another suit when that bar is irrelevant to the latter suit, and the earlier pleading reserved the right to bring the separate claim.
material_facts: An earlier suit sought protection of possession and an injunction, and its plaint referred to the oral sale agreement and reserved the right to bring a suit for specific performance.
A separate suit seeking specific performance was filed, while the suit under review sought cancellation of a later sale deed.
The High Court relied on the absence of leave under Order II Rule 2 CPC in the earlier suit to review its judgment in the cancellation suit.
The question whether the specific-performance suit was barred arose in that separate suit and was irrelevant to the cancellation suit.
issues.conclusion: The High Court's Order II Rule 2 reasoning was irrelevant to the cancellation suit and was also based on an erroneous finding that the earlier plaint had not reserved the right to sue for specific performance; it could not justify review.
issues.legal_principle: Order II Rule 2 CPC concerns the consequences of omitting a claim or part of a claim arising from the same cause of action in an earlier suit. The Court held that the bar question arose in the specific-performance suit, not in the cancellation suit, and that the earlier plaint had recorded the agreement and reserved the right to sue for specific performance. The Court also applied Order XLVII Rule 1 CPC: a review cannot rest on an alleged error that is not apparent on the record and requires examination of the pleadings and reasoning.

predicates.review_application_after_appealable_judg: A party applied to review a judgment that could have been appealed.
predicates.later_suit_claim_was_reserved_in_earlier: The earlier pleading expressly reserved the right to bring a later suit for the omitted claim.
predicates.alleged_suit_bar_concerns_a_different_pr: The asserted bar concerns a separate suit and does not bear on the claim decided in the judgment under review.

issues.definition: If a review application concerns an appealable judgment, the earlier pleading reserved the later claim, and the asserted suit bar concerns a different proceeding, that separate-suit bar cannot justify review.
